scope: Read-only final review of the three integrated production files; no source changes, no newly executed CPU tests or NPU operations.

semantic_checks.details: Only readiness flags are batched. Count snapshots remain cloned, the zero-sum startup/resume skip is identical, layers without a buffer retain top-1 fallback, statistics and histogram keys remain unchanged. Auxiliary losses and their differentiable graph are outside the modified no_grad monitoring logic.

All count buffers are read on the rank-local device before the same monitoring loop; optimizer load-balance updates run later. No buffer is mutated. Different expert-count lengths are supported because only scalar readiness results are stacked.

Unset backend preserves eager/flex/flex_cached routing. Explicit sdpa_fp32 requires eager configuration, preventing the flex_cached special branch from silently bypassing the override. One os import is present.

FP32 Q/K/V conversion, RoPE, KV cache handling and final output layout remain in the original caller. Boolean True-visible mask is expanded to [B,1,Lq,Lk]. GQA repeats match the original head ordering. Dropout stays zero, default SDPA scaling matches D**-0.5. All-masked rows use mean(V), with zero Q/K influence and uniform V contribution, retaining legacy finite-negative-mask behavior.

Existing Muon parameter assignment, algorithm, LR scaling and the AdamW algorithm remain unchanged. Constructor captures runtime foreach policy and applies it before any optimizer step, including DCP lazy state initialization. A mixed ordinary Tensor/DTensor group falls back to foreach=False without reordering or splitting groups.

The post-load hook belongs to inner AdamW. Project checkpointer expands CombinedOptimizer before set_optimizer_state_dict; installed PyTorch DCP ultimately calls inner load_state_dict. PyTorch invokes post-hooks after replacing param_groups, so the hook restores the current process policy after checkpoint override. The callback recomputes the type guard using current group.params and writes only foreach.

LR, betas, weight_decay, eps, parameter order, steps, exp_avg and exp_avg_sq are not assigned by the callback. Both False-to-True and True-to-False policies are covered by retained state-dict tests. Captured policy is stable if environment variables change later.

Monitoring defaults to 0, attention backend to empty, and NPU AdamW foreach to False. A resumed foreach value is intentionally overridden by the runtime policy even when the flag is unset, so reverting to the original execution path is effective. The existing package-availability test for platform policy is preserved.

reviewed_existing_validation.summary: Monitor 12, attention 8 plus 6 error-rule checks, AdamW 4 x 20-step cases plus builder guard 6, resume 12 all passed.
12 main-source state-dict restore cases passed; hyperparameters and moments exact.
All four main-source local/DTensor and FP32/mixed dtype cases plus builder guards passed.
Eight main-source output and Q/K/V gradient checks passed.
Nine existing NPU attention output/gradient cases passed; no new NPU run in this review.
Existing eight-rank AdamW correctness reports reviewed for pass status; no new NPU run.

non_blocking_notes: SDPA is validated within the established floating-point error budget; no bitwise identity or long-run task-quality equivalence is claimed.
The checkpoint tests exercise inner and Combined state_dict loading and static inspection confirms the real DCP path. This review did not run a fresh eight-rank end-to-end DCP save/resume.

The monitoring batching assumption is rank-local buffers on a single device, matching current eight-rank data-parallel/FSDP usage; pipeline-parallel layers distributed over devices are outside this candidate scope.
No-checkpoint configuration and seven-run throughput/memory conclusions are outside these three production code changes and are covered by separate experiment audits.
